claim: Distinctive features encode minimal phonological contrasts; phonemes can be represented as bundles of features.
source: UC Berkeley PhonLab / Sylak-Glassman dissertation discussing Jakobson-Fant-Halle distinctive features

claim: Morphemes are commonly treated as smallest meaningful units in morphology.
SFL treats language as a system of meaning-making options and distinguishes strata/functions.
source: Cambridge University Press excerpts on Systemic Functional Linguistics

claim: Codons are nucleotide triplets; 4^3 = 64 codons; 61 encode amino acids and three are stop codons in the standard code.
Six two-valued lines generate 2^6 = 64 configurations; binary encoding of the Shao Yong/Fuxi hexagram arrangement is structurally valid.
source: Cambridge Science in Context 2025; Progress in Biophysics and Molecular Biology 2017
Derived in this research by functional comparison; not a standard linguistic mapping.

claim: Primitive 64-state transition grammar is the 6-dimensional hypercube Q6 under one-line flips.
source: Direct consequence of treating each state as a six-bit vector and primitive operator as single-coordinate flip.

claim: No canonical codon↔hexagram semantic mapping follows from both having 64 states.
source: 4^3 codons versus 2^6 binary states require an arbitrary 4-symbol→2-bit bijection for one-to-one encoding.
